prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Kansas City Missouri for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one universally “best” dentist — the right choice depends on your needs (complexity of the case, bone/gum health, comfort with surgery, budget, insurance, and personal fit). Instead of a single name, it’s better to pick a provider with the right specialist training, experience in implants, and good patient outcomes.

How to find the best implant provider in Kansas City, MO
- Choose the right specialist for your situation
  - Oral & maxillofacial surgeons: ideal for surgical complexity (bone grafts, extractions, sedation, full-arch cases).
  - Periodontists: experts in gums and bone — often do implants and grafting.
  - Prosthodontists: specialists in the restoration (crowns, bridges, full-mouth implant prostheses); commonly collaborate with surgeons.
  - Some general dentists place implants, but verify experience and training.

- Credentials and experience to look for
  - Fellowship/board certification (e.g., American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, or recognized implant organizations such as AAID/ICOI).
  - Years placing implants and number of implants placed.
  - Continuing education in implantology and use of modern tech (CBCT 3D imaging, guided surgery).
  - Before/after cases or patient testimonials.

- Practical checks
  - Request a consult and CBCT-based treatment plan.
  - Ask what implant brands they use and why.
  - Ask about sedation/anesthesia options and infection/safety protocols.
  - Verify warranties, follow-up schedule, and who handles complications.
  - Compare total cost (implant + abutment + crown + any grafting) — typical US single-tooth implant costs often range roughly $3,000–$6,000, more with grafting or specialty components.

Where to look and verify
- AAID and ADA “Find a Dentist” directories.
- Board certification directories for OMS/periodontists/prosthodontists.
- Local reviews: Google, Yelp, Healthgrades — pay attention to details in reviews (results, communication, complications handling).
- Ask your general dentist for a referral — they often know reputable specialists locally.

Important questions to ask at the consult
- How many implants like mine have you placed?
- Are you board-certified or a fellow of any implant organizations?
- Do you use CBCT scans and guided implant placement?
- What implant brand will you use and why?
- Who will restore the crown — you or another dentist?
- What are the risks and success rates for cases like mine?
- Can you show before/after photos and patient references?
- What is the total cost and payment/insurance options?

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft a short list of questions to ask at a consult or a message to send to offices.
- Evaluate a few dentist names or clinic websites you find and point out red flags or positives.

If you give me your ZIP code or the neighborhood in Kansas City you prefer, I’ll guide you on how to narrow the search and what to look for locally.
